details: The cryptocurrency industry has spent approximately $176 million across over 100 U.S. midterm election races in an effort to build a bipartisan coalition in Congress and secure clearer regulatory rules. This strategic spending aims to shape future policy beyond the current administration. Separately, a cyberattack on the Federal Election Commission temporarily concealed last-minute political spending by large donors, adding opacity to election financing as the midterms draw near.
title: Crypto Industry Pours $176M into US Midterms Amid Cyberattack

details: Argentinian President Javier Milei and his sister Karina Milei have been cleared of fraud in a high-profile memecoin scandal. A federal judge dismissed the criminal investigation, finding no evidence of a fraudulent scheme despite the "Libra" token's dramatic collapse after Milei promoted it on social media in February 2025.
title: Argentine President Milei Cleared in Memecoin Scandal

details: The ongoing Middle East conflict, including hostilities involving Saudi Arabia and Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis, continues to keep oil prices elevated due to concerns over supply disruptions. Brent crude futures were around $115-$116 a barrel on October 28. On October 29, oil prices saw a slight decline as "peace hopes offset fears of growing Middle East conflict" after Qatari mediators presented a new draft peace deal to Iran. However, a senior Iranian official has reportedly dismissed these as "unacceptable ideas." The World Bank projects global commodity prices, particularly energy, to surge by 23% in 2026, with Brent crude averaging $91 per barrel, citing the Middle East conflict and Black Sea disruptions.
sourceName: Al Jazeera / Investing.com (citing Reuters) / World Bank
title: Middle East Conflict Keeps Oil Prices Volatile, Peace Hopes Emerge

details: Russia has resumed grain shipments through the Sea of Azov after a three-month suspension caused by Ukrainian drone attacks. The previous halt had negatively impacted Russia's economy and contributed to an increase in global grain prices. This comes amidst reports that Sberbank's bad loans in Russia have risen by nearly 20%, indicating deepening economic troubles with forecasts for prolonged sluggish growth.
title: Russia Resumes Grain Shipments Through Sea of Azov
